title: ROS production, scavenging and redox buffering

nodes.label: Complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase)
nodes.rationale: The FMN site forms a flavin semiquinone during turnover and is a known superoxide-producing leak site, and the Fe/S chain performs sequential one-electron transfers — both of the physical routes the radical-pair and hyperfine arguments require. No published experiment has applied a near-null field and measured plant complex I activity, so this is a hypothesis with a mechanism, not a result.
nodes.caveat: Electron transfer along the Fe/S chain is fast relative to plausible singlet-triplet mixing times, so a coherent radical-pair effect here is harder to argue than at the flavin. Treat the flavin and the cluster chain as separate hypotheses rather than one.

nodes.label: Plastid superoxide / H2O2
nodes.rationale: As in the mitochondrion, the amplifier rather than the mechanism: threshold behaviour converts a small change in electron branching into a signal.

evidence.claim: Reactive oxygen species production differed between geomagnetic and near-null field conditions in lima bean.
Near-null magnetic field alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis.

nodes.label: Peroxisomal beta-oxidation
nodes.rationale: Acyl-CoA oxidase is a flavoprotein that reduces O2 directly to H2O2 as part of its normal catalytic cycle — one of the few places in the cell where peroxide production is the intended chemistry rather than a leak. During germination that makes the peroxisome a major ROS source at exactly the stage the review argues matters most.
nodes.caveat: A flavin semiquinone is not well established in the acyl-CoA oxidase mechanism, and the enzyme's own catalase-rich compartment quenches the product quickly. Classed only as a ROS source, not as a radical-pair site.

nodes.label: Mitochondrial superoxide / H2O2
nodes.rationale: Not a magnetosensitive mechanism itself — it is the amplifier. A field effect too small to measure as a rate change can still register here, because ROS signalling is threshold-like.

evidence.claim: Near-null magnetic field exposure alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis.
Reactive oxygen species and mitochondria jointly regulate seed germination, establishing the route from mitochondrial ROS to a developmental outcome.

nodes.label: Ascorbate peroxidase (APX1, APX2)
nodes.rationale: Catalysis proceeds through Compound I, an oxoferryl porphyrin pi-cation radical — a genuine protein-based radical intermediate, and one of the few in the redox network rather than the electron transport chains.
nodes.caveat: The porphyrin radical is strongly exchange-coupled to the ferryl iron and extremely short-lived. Structurally it is a radical; whether it could ever be a spin-correlated pair with a geomagnetically relevant lifetime is untested and doubtful.

nodes.label: Catalase (CAT1, CAT2, CAT3)
nodes.rationale: Like ascorbate peroxidase, catalase cycles through a Compound I porphyrin radical. Its relevance here is positional: it is the enzyme standing between germination beta-oxidation and oxidative damage.

nodes.label: Ascorbate-glutathione cycle (GR1, DHAR1, MDAR1)
nodes.rationale: Glutathione reductase and monodehydroascorbate reductase are FAD enzymes, so the same flavin semiquinone chemistry applies here as at complex I and FNR. MDAR is notable for acting on a stable organic radical — monodehydroascorbate — as its actual substrate.
nodes.caveat: The monodehydroascorbate radical is free in solution rather than held in a protein pocket, so it has no correlated partner and tumbles freely. It is a radical, not a radical pair.

nodes.label: ROS-responsive transcriptional programme
nodes.rationale: This entity carries demonstrated near-null-field evidence but NO proposed quantum route, and is classed structural_context to say so explicitly. It is the amplifier's output: threshold-like signalling turns an upstream change too small to measure directly into a transcriptional response. That sensitivity is what makes it the best-evidenced node in the atlas and simultaneously a poor discriminator — it reports that something moved upstream, never what.

evidence.claim: Transcriptomics and metabolomics of ROS modulation in near-null magnetic field-induced Arabidopsis: field reduction alters ROS-associated transcriptional and metabolic programmes.
Arabidopsis PPR40 connects abiotic stress responses to mitochondrial electron transport, establishing a route from respiratory state to stress signalling.
